sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Envirotech Systems Limited is a small, project-led manufacturer and installer of industrial acoustic enclosures, barriers, silencers, doors and testing environments. This is a capacity-ramp and potential value thesis, not a demonstrated compounder. Its strongest evidence is real revenue growth and an established engineering business: revenue increased from ₹18.11 crore in FY22 to ₹57.59 crore in FY26, with identifiable new orders from Gainwell Commosales and Utkal Alumina before the research cutoff. The decisive weakness is that accounting earnings have not become dependable cash for common shareholders. Receivables reached ₹31.71 crore, inventories ₹9.67 crore and additional property advances ₹5.84 crore. The enlarged factory has absorbed substantial capital without yet establishing mature incremental returns. [S1 pp97–125; S2 printed pp185–200; S10–S11 pp1–2.]

At the verified 19 October 2026 close of ₹55.85, market capitalization is ₹104.94 crore. Reported FY26 P/E of 8.67 times and operating EV/EBITDA of 6.24 times look modest, but neither measures the working-capital burden or proves that expansion is currently funded. An explicitly conditional base model produces a 14.11% five-year annualized return, below the requested 15% nominal pre-personal-tax hurdle. That is not a supported investment return: the latest balance sheet is March 2026, bank drawings and drawing power at the October cutoff are unknown, and remaining completion costs are assumptions. R and IAS therefore remain NS. [S1 pp97–102,114; S3–S4; model/results.json.]

Business Quality is 4.8/10, with an exact unrounded score of 4.78. Growth Quality is 5.0/10 after the persistent poor-cash-conversion cap, compared with raw 6.05. These quality scores remain available for cautious comparison because the identified accounting presentation differences have been bounded sufficiently for historical economics; G3 Hold is not itself a quality-ranking exclusion. Current funding, not a low share price, is the missing investability condition. The appropriate action is a research hold for new capital, not an accusation of fraud or a declaration of insolvency. A verified collection improvement, documented working-capital headroom, completed operating permissions and returns from the new plant could change the assessment. A cheaper quote alone would not resolve those gaps. The two most uncertain historical factor judgments can move BQS by 0.32 point jointly, so nearby rankings should be treated as ties rather than precise distinctions.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factor scores are GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 4, CASH 3, BAL 4, EXEC 4 and EARN 5. The investment factors are R NS, D 3, P 4 and L 4. Every factor has separate facts, contrary evidence, confidence and evidence IDs in the machine-readable audit. These are judgment scores under one common framework, not statistical estimates. CAP uses additional operating capital, not current ROCE. EARN addresses recurring operating and per-share profit, whereas CASH addresses realization; the same rationale is not simply copied between them.

BQS is 0.20×4 + 0.20×5 + 0.12×8 + 0.10×6 + 0.12×4 + 0.10×3 + 0.08×4 + 0.08×4 = 4.78. Its coverage is 100%, no governance or funding-failure cap applies, and its final display is 4.8. GQS means Growth Quality. It is 0.40×8 + 0.20×6 + 0.15×5 + 0.15×4 + 0.10×3 = 6.05. Persistent poor cash realization triggers the explicit cap at 5, giving final 5.0. A temporary factory ramp alone would not justify that cap; the cross-period collection evidence does. No additional discretionary growth bonus is added for data centers, customer names or a new factory. [E3–E9.]

IAS reuses unrounded final BQS exactly once. Its known contribution is 0.25×4.78 + 0.20×3 + 0.10×4 + 0.10×4 = 2.595. R's original 35% weight remains missing. Coverage is 65%; the mathematical completion interval is [2.595 + 0.35×1, 2.595 + 0.35×10] = [2.945, 6.095], displayed 2.9–6.1 with half-up rounding. sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Envirotech sells engineered noise-control systems rather than a recurring software subscription, a water-treatment concession or an environmental commodity. Products include acoustic enclosures for generators and industrial machinery, noise barriers, acoustic doors and partitions, silencers and specialized test rooms. Its economic work combines design, material procurement, fabrication, installation and acceptance at a customer site. Revenue therefore depends on project timing, site readiness and performance requirements. A customer relationship may repeat, but there is no disclosed annuity-like contracted renewal base that warrants treating every project as recurring revenue. [S1 business discussion pp4–7,76–82; S2 business section printed pp123–139.]

The firm earns by converting acoustic engineering and manufactured assemblies into accepted customer installations. Steel, insulation, fabrication labor, bought-out components and freight are important inputs. The acoustic system must reduce noise while preserving ventilation, maintenance access, fire safety and equipment performance. Successful delivery can create qualification and reference advantages. It does not automatically confer pricing power across all tenders. Tender awards, installation progress, invoicing, retention and cash collection can be separated by months, which explains why a healthy operating margin is not a substitute for a cash-cycle analysis.

The September 2026 Gainwell order is especially informative about the product: ₹2.925 crore excluding tax covers acoustic enclosures for two CAT 3,000 KVA generator sets, associated acoustic partition work and installation for the Sify Infinity Data Centre project. The October Utkal Alumina order is ₹2.2671576 crore inclusive of all taxes, with dispatches scheduled by December 2026 and January 2027 and installation by June 2027. These are different tax bases and should not be added into an exact revenue backlog. Both disclosures deny promoter interest and related-party status for the transaction. They evidence accessible industrial demand, not completed sales or collected profits. [S10–S11 pp1–2.]

The manufacturing expansion at the D-3 Greater Noida site is central to the next stage. FY26 closing fixed assets and work in progress together are ₹45.31 crore, compared with ₹38.46 crore a year earlier. A large transfer from construction to operating assets is visible, and depreciation rises sharply. Management nevertheless described partial commissioning and outstanding permissions on the May 2026 call. No later primary evidence in the retained set establishes full commercial readiness of every line by the cutoff. Potential fire-door, solar-barrier, defense, semiconductor and data-center opportunities are distinct products and qualifications, not an already proven common revenue engine. The accounts do not provide sufficiently consistent product-level revenue, margin or geography tables for a precise segment mix. In particular, the detailed goods-revenue line contains a digit inconsistency with the audited total. This report uses the reconciled total and leaves the mix unquantified. [S1 pp98,118–124; S8 pp2–3.]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is accumulated design competence, fabrication integration, acoustic testing and delivery references. A large industrial buyer must trust that an enclosure will meet noise criteria without damaging equipment operation; a proven supplier may face lower qualification friction on a repeat contract. Custom engineering, site coordination and fit-for-purpose manufacturing are more defensible than distributing generic sound-absorbing sheets. The two recent orders and the operating history provide evidence that Envirotech can win relevant work. They do not establish dominant market share, exclusive technology, contract lock-in or persistent pricing power. MOAT 5 reflects a useful but contestable capability. [S2 business and risk sections; S10–S11.]

Three economically relevant reference competitors are IAC Acoustics, Acoustics India Private Limited and Ecotone Systems. Their official product materials describe comparable industrial enclosures, noise-control installations or specialized acoustic environments. IAC illustrates the broader engineered-system competitor; Acoustics India provides an Indian industrial application comparator; Ecotone demonstrates nearby Indian competition across enclosures and barriers. These are product and capability comparisons only. Their ownership, reporting perimeter and available public economics are not sufficiently comparable to manufacture a listed peer P/E or ROIC table. The prospectus also names large insulation suppliers such as Saint-Gobain and Rockwool in its industry discussion; these are not clean pure-play system-integrator valuation peers. [S18–S20; S2 industry section.]

Concentration weakens bargaining power. The prospectus reports top-ten customer shares of 43.26%, 26.83% and 50.43% in FY22, FY23 and FY24. The non-monotonic pattern demonstrates project mix rather than a stable recurring cohort. Top-ten suppliers account for 73.35%, 54.53% and 50.10% across those years, and long-term supply arrangements are not assured. Current FY26 customer concentration and customer-level collections are not disclosed in the retained evidence. It would be wrong to apply FY24 concentration as if it were current, but equally wrong to infer that rapid growth has diversified the book. [S2 printed pp24–25,227.]

The main moat failure modes are a qualified competitor undercutting price, buyers internalizing enclosure fabrication, loss of a key technical team, input inflation during fixed-price execution, or an installation failing acceptance. Regulation may stimulate demand for noise control but is not a patent owned by Envirotech. Growth into fire-rated doors introduces another certification and execution burden, not a free extension of existing expertise. No independently verified market-share series, unit-price premium, renewal retention curve or tender win-rate supports a high moat score. Contrary evidence is that sophisticated customers still issue project-specific purchase orders and payment remains slow despite claimed customer quality. The absence of a clean quoted peer universe is a valuation limitation, not a reason to award a premium by analogy with unrelated listed environmental businesses.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The comparable standalone revenue series is ₹9.8123 crore in FY21, ₹18.1065 crore in FY22, ₹28.3178 crore in FY23, ₹46.2398 crore in FY24, ₹47.6117 crore in FY25 and ₹57.5876 crore in FY26. Annual rupee additions from FY22 onward are ₹8.2942, ₹10.2113, ₹17.9220, ₹1.3719 and ₹9.9759 crore. FY25 growth was only 2.97%, followed by FY26 growth of 20.95%; the latest year is a recovery in additions, not evidence of an uninterrupted 40% run rate. There is no identified acquisition in this period requiring a perimeter subtraction. Price, volume and project mix are not separately quantified, so “same-company growth” is supportable while “entirely volume-driven organic growth” is not. [S1 p99; S2 printed pp185–187; S6 financial statements; S16 FY21 statements.]

Endpoint calculations give 42.47% over FY21–FY26, 26.69% over FY23–FY26 and 11.60% over FY24–FY26. The five-year start is the pandemic trough. FY20 revenue was approximately ₹15.7151 crore, making the six-year FY20–FY26 CAGR 24.17%, a materially less spectacular through-disruption comparison. The selected canonical revenue score uses the three-year FY23–FY26 CAGR of 26.69%, producing a base score of 8 under the common schedule. No trajectory adjustment is added: the two most recent years do not establish growth above the selected band, and the pandemic distortion is already handled by the selected window. Medium confidence and the uneven cycle also prevent a 9–10 score. [S16; model/historical.csv.]

Growth is not only a percentage. FY26's ₹9.98 crore addition was supported by a much larger asset and inventory base, while FY24 had added ₹17.92 crore on far less capital. This does not prove the new plant will fail, because assets can precede sales, but it is the relevant scale comparison. To achieve the conditional base model's terminal revenue of about ₹105.09 crore, the company must add roughly ₹47.50 crore to FY26 sales. The model does not import management's earlier ₹100 crore FY26 target as an achieved run rate. Nor does it extrapolate a single announced purchase order into the whole factory's utilization. [S1 pp97–125; S7 pp4–5; model/results.json.]

Management's May 2025 discussion pointed toward ₹100 crore FY26 revenue and much larger potential capacity after commissioning. Actual FY26 sales fell about 42.41% below that ₹100 crore aspiration. The May 2026 call acknowledged disappointment and avoided a fresh precise revenue promise. This is meaningful evidence about forecast reliability and EXEC, while the audited revenue history still independently earns REV 8. Demand access has improved through identifiable industrial customers, but the amount converted into accepted, paid revenue is the central test. Updated September-half results were not available by the cutoff in the retained set; no subsequent period's financial information is silently incorporated.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
There are identifiable demand avenues: industrial noise compliance, generator installations for data centers, road or industrial barriers, testing facilities and potentially fire-rated doors. Actual disclosed customer orders are better evidence of accessible demand than a broad market-size estimate. However, a project-led manufacturer needs qualifications, operating permissions, labor, material purchasing and collection funding before that demand becomes economic growth. Management's ₹200–250 crore potential full-operation revenue discussion is a capacity aspiration, not an order book, guaranteed utilization level or independently verified nameplate output. The model treats it as an upside ceiling reference and does not value it as an asset in addition to forecast earnings. [S7 pp4–5; S8 pp2–6; S10–S11.]

The bottom-up question is how incremental sales become cash and additional operating profit. FY26 net fixed assets, construction and software development total ₹45.31 crore; property advances add ₹5.84 crore, and operating working capital defined in the model is ₹36.93 crore. The latter includes receivables, inventory, operating advances and prepayments less trade and recurring operating liabilities. Deposits and opening claims are separately classified. Operating capital is approximately ₹87.80 crore after excluding cash, fixed deposits, tax assets and unamortized IPO expenses and including relevant non-interest-bearing tax funding. An independently constructed asset-side bridge matches the funding-side result to ₹0.000021 crore, attributable to published rounding. This is the denominator relevant to reinvestment, not merely equity book value. [S1 pp97–125; model/results.json.]

Normalized NOPAT uses operating EBIT excluding all other income, multiplied by 74%, with a common 26% tax assumption. From FY23 to FY26 annual NOPAT increases by ₹10.5547 crore while operating capital increases by ₹71.6215 crore, giving a 14.74% firm-wide incremental-return proxy. FY24–FY26 gives only 2.63%; FY25–FY26 gives 9.22%. A reasoned 13–18% nominal cost-of-capital range is a research sensitivity for a small, concentrated and illiquid project business, not a quoted company WACC or the separate 15% equity hurdle. The three-year proxy is around that range, while recent capital vintages have earned less. CAP 4 reflects weak recent returns with an immature ramp, not a neutral default and not a conclusion that lifetime project IRR equals 2.63%. [E8.]

The latest year's ₹21.3133 crore incremental operating capital comprises approximately ₹6.8466 crore net fixed-asset expansion, ₹5.8378 crore property advances and ₹8.6289 crore working-capital and other operating movements. This bridge prevents attributing all new capital to the factory alone. Unit economics by product, capacity cohort and accepted order are unavailable; the aggregate proxy cannot separate early-stage investment from deterioration in mature contracts. The new factory could improve the result through utilization and throughput, but sustained collections must accompany utilization. The conditional model therefore includes additional completion spending, maintenance and growth capex, working-capital ratios, interest, tax and dilution rather than capitalizing sales targets at an unchanged share count.

Raw GQS of 6.05 is dominated by demonstrated revenue growth, not by proven reinvestment excellence. CASH 3 caps final GQS at 5.0 because poor realization persists across multiple annual observations and remains weak even after classification sensitivities. A sustainable runway would require at least two reporting periods of stronger collections, a credible remaining-capex budget, operational permissions, and improving incremental earnings on the enlarged capital base. Until then the business has capacity and demand opportunities, but it has not demonstrated a self-replenishing growth engine. There is no evidence-based reason to call it a compounder simply because revenue can plausibly grow faster than the broader economy.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Manoj Kumar Gupta and Sindhu Gupta held 48.72% and 20.13%, respectively, at March 2026, approximately 68.85% combined. The retained March shareholding pattern reports no promoter pledge. A later September filing confirms Manoj's open-market purchase of 9,000 shares on 29 September; it is not treated as a complete updated ownership register, and no post-March percentage is fabricated. High promoter ownership and small purchases may align incentives, but neither proves cash quality or minority fairness. [S1 p113; S12; S13 p1 and Form C.]

Promoter managerial remuneration increased from ₹0.54 crore in FY25 to ₹0.84 crore in FY26, a 55.56% increase while PAT declined. It is about 6.94% of PAT and exceeds reported operating cash flow. Loans received from these two related parties during FY26 totaled ₹1.48195 crore, and the same amount was repaid; no closing related-party borrowing is reported. These are disclosed cash movements, not automatically diversion. The September AGM approved the managing director's terms and the corrected employee-option scheme. The incentive pool permits up to 939,500 options, equivalent to 5% of existing shares, but permission to grant is not proof that the entire pool is outstanding. Exercise terms vary with timing and valuation, with a ₹10 minimum; the model explicitly labels full-pool exercise at that minimum as a conservative scenario, not a verified grant ledger. [S1 pp109,113–114; S14–S15.]

The earlier statutory auditor resigned in October 2024 because the firm lacked the peer-review qualification needed after listing; the resignation letter does not identify a dispute or another adverse reason. HCO's FY26 opinion is unmodified. This is a positive counterweight to disclosure concerns. The FY26 secretarial audit nevertheless records delays and omissions in specified exchange or structured-digital-database filings. Financial-statement templates contain the wrong company name in the internal-controls annexure, inconsistent year labels, CSR-unit errors and digit mistakes in detailed schedules. These reduce reporting discipline; the analysis does not elevate them into a proven fraud allegation. The ₹0.15168 crore penal-charge line in finance costs deserves an explanation, even though the audit does not report a borrowing default. [S1 pp74,86–96,109,121,125; S9.]

The promises-versus-delivery record is unfavorable on timing. In May 2025, management discussed full expanded operation around December 2025 and approximately ₹100 crore FY26 sales. The audited outcome was ₹57.59 crore; the May 2026 call described partial commissioning and pending permissions. The new order disclosures in September and October show continuing demand access, but they do not erase the commissioning and sales shortfall. The May 2026 decision not to give another precise numerical promise is more prudent than recycling the old target, yet it leaves forecasting less anchored. EXEC 4 recognizes an operating business and real sales alongside a material miss, rather than treating every announced capacity milestone as completed. [S7 pp4–5,12; S8 pp2,5–6; S10–S11.]

The stewardship test is whether cash now goes into completing productive assets and collecting existing work before another cycle of property advances or expansion. No dividend is assumed: the FY26 reserves schedule shows no distribution and the business has immediate reinvestment demands. The next decisive governance evidence would be clean reconciliations, complete current bank and option disclosures, reasons for penal charges, and customer collection information. GOV 4 is a cautious judgment about controls and capital allocation; it is above the severe-adverse-evidence threshold, so no governance override is manufactured.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The five-year core table is reproduced in model/historical.csv, with FY21 included as an additional pandemic reference. FY22–FY26 revenue is ₹18.1065 / ₹28.3178 / ₹46.2398 / ₹47.6117 / ₹57.5876 crore; operating EBITDA excluding all other income is ₹1.5758 / ₹3.6272 / ₹15.9612 / ₹15.3302 / ₹19.0389 crore. Reported PAT is ₹1.0573 / ₹2.5734 / ₹11.4288 / ₹14.0578 / ₹12.1056 crore. Revenue and profit therefore tell different recent stories. FY25 other income contains a ₹3.875808 crore property-sale profit. Removing that gain at the common 26% tax assumption reduces FY25 PAT to approximately ₹11.1897 crore, making FY26 normalized progress about 8.18%, rather than the reported PAT decline of 13.89%. This normalization is analytical, not an audited restatement; the actual tax attached to the disposal is not separately established. [S1 pp99,123; S2 printed pp185–200; S6 financials.]

FY26 EBITDA is reconstructed as PBT ₹16.989507 + finance cost ₹1.374135 + depreciation ₹1.269172 − other income ₹0.593919 = ₹19.038895 crore. EBIT is ₹17.769723 crore. The annual report reallocates ₹0.223081 crore between other income and other expenses relative to the May results without changing PBT or PAT. Using the later audited report's presentation is consistent, but a purported margin improvement based on mixing the two versions would be false. Material contribution before labor and other production costs can be calculated from revenue less materials and stock changes, but that is not a clean disclosed gross profit; no invented gross-margin series is used. [S1 pp99,123–126; S17 financial statements.]

Cash realization is much weaker. Reported CFO for FY22–FY26 on the latest available statutory presentation is ₹1.5481 / −₹0.0979 / −₹1.5334 / −₹1.3631 / ₹0.5040 crore. Cash capex is ₹0.3635 / ₹6.5436 / ₹0.1712 / ₹28.5891 / ₹7.7541 crore. Corresponding FCF proxies are ₹1.1846 / −₹6.6415 / −₹1.7046 / −₹29.9522 / −₹7.2501 crore. These must not be interpreted without the classification bridge. The prospectus reports FY24 CFO of ₹4.8861 crore because loan-and-advance movements were presented in financing. Moving ₹6.419503 crore of those movements into operations explains the later negative comparator. Most of that movement relates to property advances. FY25 CFO was originally −₹1.015613 crore and is −₹1.363122 crore in the FY26 comparative; investing and financing lines also change, largely offsetting at total-cash level. The remaining ₹0.347509 crore CFO presentation change requires a formal explanation rather than being silently replaced. The FY25 investing section also labels an amount equal to the property-sale profit as net sale proceeds; without the disposal-cost bridge, that is not evidence that profit and gross cash proceeds are economically identical. [S2 printed pp187,199; S6 cash flow and notes; S1 pp101–102.]

The latest three-year ratio of summed CFO to summed PAT is −6.36% on those statutory presentations. Using the prospectus FY24 classification instead gives 10.71%, not a robust cash-compounding result either. A further property-transfer sensitivity moves the FY24 property advance into investing, reverses the FY25 non-cash transfer release, and treats FY26 property advances as investing. Together with the inventory/CWIP reclassification described below, this produces only about 10.13% conversion. This is a cash-neutral diagnostic, not a substitute audited cash-flow statement. It is why CASH 3 and the GQS cap do not depend on selecting the harshest accounting classification. [E4–E7.]

FY26 CFO is traceable: PBT ₹16.989506 + depreciation ₹1.269172, less receivable growth ₹4.171616, other-current-asset use ₹0.729765, inventory use ₹6.394879 and advances use ₹6.189955, plus other-current-liability growth ₹0.568078, trade-payable growth ₹1.664460, provisions ₹0.609202 and other-non-current-asset release ₹0.159590, less interest income ₹0.212284 and tax paid ₹3.057512, yields ₹0.503997 crore, within rounding of reported CFO. The new ₹5.8378 crore property advance is economically significant even though it sits within an advances line rather than cash capex. FY26 net fixed-asset growth plus depreciation is ₹8.115768 crore, versus reported cash capex of ₹7.754089 crore. The ₹0.361679 crore difference matches the inventory-to-CWIP shift between May results and the annual report. Moving that amount from operating to investing cash flow raises CFO and capex equally, leaving FCF unchanged. It does not create extra cash. [S1 pp98,101,118,120; S17 balance sheet.]

Average-balance receivable days rise from about 118.1 in FY24 to 175.4 in FY25 and 187.7 in FY26. The FY26 ending-balance measure is roughly 201 days and is not mislabeled as the average. Closing receivables include ₹11.93 crore in the total-row buckets older than six months and approximately ₹6.49 crore older than a year. Doubtful-classified balances total ₹0.459578 crore. The detailed good-receivable row has obvious missing-digit inconsistencies, while the age-column total and balance-sheet aggregate reconcile. Accordingly the report uses the reconciled total row and requests a customer-level aging and allowance bridge; it does not silently repair the printed “good” row or assume doubtful amounts have already been fully provided. Inventory increases from ₹3.64 crore to ₹9.67 crore, with substantial work in progress and finished goods. High customer quality does not remove acceptance, retention or collection risk. [S1 pp120–124.]

Gross debt increases from ₹8.16 crore to ₹13.94 crore, predominantly working-capital banks. The ₹0.063654 crore current vehicle maturity is already included in short-term debt, not counted twice. Cash on hand and current-account balances total only ₹0.084697 crore. Fixed deposits of approximately ₹2.422941 crore are separately identified; historical deposits were under lien, and current release conditions are not established, so ordinary scenarios do not call them freely available. Net debt excluding those deposits is ₹13.85 crore, roughly 0.73 times operating EBITDA, and operating EBIT covers reported finance costs about 12.93 times. Those reassuring accrual ratios coexist with weak cash conversion and demand-repayable bank debt. [S1 pp102,114,121–122; S2 printed p199.]

The funding model pays opening net income-tax claims of ₹1.758037 crore, current gratuity ₹0.061750 crore and credit-card payable ₹0.007631 crore once in year one. Tax assets are assumed offsettable against the same issuer's tax provision; failure of that assumption adds ₹2.366794 crore to required liquidity. Trade creditors, customer advances and ordinary payroll/statutory balances remain within operating working capital, not additional terminal debt. This assumes ordinary operating turnover rather than overdue statutory liabilities being indefinitely ignored. Security deposit liabilities, long-term gratuity and a conservative deferred-tax reserve are deducted once at terminal value. Related-party loans have no closing balance; FY26 lease/rent expense of ₹0.201021 crore remains in operating expenses. Leases are not separately quantified as financing debt in the retained accounts, so no undisclosed financing lease is invented or inconsistently added to EBITDA. [S1 pp114–117.]

Current issued shares are 1.879 crore. FY26 reported basic and diluted EPS are ₹6.44; the FY26 annual report shows ₹7.48 for FY25 using its presented comparator. The prospectus prints earlier basic/diluted EPS of ₹21.15, ₹51.47 and ₹8.54 for FY22–FY24 on stated denominators of 0.05, 0.05 and 1.339 crore shares; the 25:1 bonus and subsequent issues make those raw per-share numbers incomparable. The model retains them separately and uses current-share-equivalent earnings for a common-denominator comparison. For valuation it uses actual current issued capital and separately tests the option pool, rather than importing a historical weighted denominator. No acquisition goodwill, minority interest or subsidiary earnings bridge is needed. Unamortized IPO costs of approximately ₹2.37317 crore are excluded from operating capital and are not treated as a cash-like asset in terminal equity. Average-capital normalized ROIC falls from approximately 49.35% in FY24 to 22.93% in FY25 and 17.05% in FY26, but these current/average ratios are context only. The CAP score comes from the explicit incremental-capital bridge in section 7.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹55.85 and 1.879 crore issued shares, market capitalization is ₹104.94215 crore. Adding ₹13.935565 crore gross debt and subtracting ₹0.084697 crore cash gives enterprise value ₹118.793018 crore, or 6.24 times FY26 operating EBITDA. Treating all ₹2.422941 crore fixed deposits as freely available reduces EV to ₹116.370077 crore; that is a sensitivity, not the central cash definition. Reported P/E is 8.67 times and P/B is approximately 1.38 times. FY26 FCF yield is negative, roughly −6.91%, so the low P/E is not equivalent to a current distributable cash yield. Book value includes property, working capital and deferred expenses rather than independently realizable liquidation proceeds. [S1 pp97–125; S3–S4.]

The intrinsic return model follows five annual operating and funding bridges rather than merely multiplying future EPS. Bear revenue growth is 0%, then 5% annually; operating EBITDA margin is 22%, working capital 75% of revenue, additional completion capex ₹4 crore plus 3% of annual sales, and terminal EV/EBITDA four times. Base growth is 15%, 15%, 12%, 12% and 10%; margin is 29%, working-capital ratios improve from 65% to 60%, completion capex is ₹3 crore plus 3% of sales each year, and terminal multiple is six times. Bull growth is 25%, 25%, 20%, 20% and 18%; margin is 31%, working capital 55%, completion spending ₹5 crore plus 4% of sales annually, and terminal multiple eight times. These are analyst assumptions, not management guidance. The base multiple is below the current 6.24 times rather than relying on rerating. [Model inputs and annual CSVs.]

All cases use depreciation at 2.5% of sales, 26% cash tax on positive operating profit after interest, 12% debt interest, a ₹0.25 crore operating cash floor and no dividend. Existing vehicle debt is repaid over the first two years under an explicit accelerated assumption; current bank debt is conditionally rolled, with no additional ordinary draw. Retained surplus is added at terminal equity and is not also distributed as a dividend. The full authorized option pool is assumed exercised only at the endpoint at ₹10, adding ₹0.9395 crore cash and increasing shares to 1.97295 crore. Actual grants, vesting and exercise timing remain unknown. No option proceeds fund the early cash bridge. Ordinary cases include no new external equity or rescue borrowing.

Terminal revenue is approximately ₹70.00 / ₹105.09 / ₹152.89 crore for bear/base/bull. The base funds about ₹15.85 crore of modeled capex and ₹26.12 crore incremental working capital, ending with ₹44.66 crore cash and ₹13.74 crore debt. After other claims and option proceeds, its terminal value is ₹108.06 per diluted share, implying 14.11% annualized before personal taxes and transaction costs. Bull's corresponding conditional value is ₹209.26 and 30.24%. These are internally consistent conditional calculations, not supported investable returns, because current bank rollover, cash availability and completion obligations are unverified. Even base year-one cash is only ₹0.495 crore, leaving a modest cushion above the chosen cash floor. A positive illustrative cash path does not make G3 Pass or R scoreable.

Bear becomes cash-negative in the first two years and requires ₹5.7034 crore gross hypothetical equity at 70% of the entry quote with 3% issuance costs to preserve the cash floor. Without that financing, ordinary investor IRR is null; its arithmetic terminal diagnostic is not advertised as a return. In the separately labeled equity-rescue case, dilution and proceeds are both modeled, producing terminal price ₹32.80 and approximately −10.10% annualized, a 41.27% price decline from entry. This is not a committed financing proposal. A five-year scenario cannot repair an early payment failure by pretending that later profits were available in year one. [model/results.json, cases and hypothetical_equity_rescue.]

The reverse calculation asks what growth is needed with base margin, working-capital improvement and six-times exit EBITDA. Constant annual growth of about 14.09% reaches the 15% hurdle, with terminal sales about ₹111.34 crore. Hurdles of 12% and 18% require about 10.43% and 17.85% growth; the high-hurdle path also requires hypothetical early equity, which remains explicit. The base-path entry prices for 12%, 15% and 18% are approximately ₹61.32, ₹53.72 and ₹47.23. These are assumption-dependent calculations, not a recommendation that ₹53.72 resolves funding risk. Base return falls to about 13.66%, 12.75% and 11.85% if entry and exit each cost 1%, 3% and 5%, respectively. Actual bid-ask spreads and impact are unavailable. [Model reverse and cost sensitivities.]

A growth-versus-exit-multiple matrix is provided in the model. At constant 10% growth, conditional returns are about 4.51%, 11.65% and 17.33% at four, six and eight times EBITDA. At 15% growth they are about 7.98%, 15.75% and 21.86%. Thus a respectable growth story still fails the hurdle if the market normalizes to a lower multiple. A relevant earnings cross-check is the reported 8.67-times P/E, normalized FY25 profit and the declining incremental-return record, not a borrowed multiple from an unrelated water-infrastructure issuer. Omitting the option pool raises the base return to about 15.13%, showing that dilution alone can change a borderline classification. No numerical forecast deserves to hide that sensitivity.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument is not that noise-control demand disappears. It is that an engineering company with attractive reported margins becomes structurally capital hungry as projects, inventories, receivables and property commitments grow together. Customers may be creditworthy yet slow to approve or pay; the manufacturer pays labor, suppliers, taxes and banks before acceptance. If the expanded facility fails to generate enough throughput, fixed costs and depreciation rise while working capital remains trapped. Current accounting earnings then overstate the cash that common equity can receive. This is a High impairment-risk situation in the model, although the evidence does not establish present insolvency or actual borrowing default. [S1 pp97–125; S7–S8.]

The linked stress tests quantify the mechanism. Losing just 5% of FY26 receivables, ₹1.5853 crore, turns base year-one cash from positive ₹0.4954 crore to negative ₹1.0899 crore. Requiring repayment of 25% of the ₹13.7361 crore working-capital bank borrowing similarly creates approximately ₹2.9386 crore negative cash before any rescue. These are cash losses or debt repayments modeled once, not arbitrary additional discounts to the same terminal value. Failure to use the opening tax credits creates another ₹2.3668 crore liquidity requirement. The future collection and funding assumptions are therefore the important sensitivity, not only a one-point terminal multiple change. [Model linked_stresses and opening-claims bridge.]

The ordinary bear case has no valid investor return because it runs out of modeled cash. Its separate equity-rescue outcome of about ₹32.80 is useful for downside illustration, but an actual raise could be unavailable, slower, more dilutive or conditioned on new security. Existing owners bear dilution or residual-claim loss after banks, tax authorities, employees and suppliers. Plant and land may preserve some recovery, but no independent liquidation appraisal, enforceable sale timetable or lien-priority analysis supports a hard share-price floor. Receivables marked doubtful and opaque aging schedules are not cash collateral at face value. The rescue sensitivity is therefore not a maximum-loss estimate.

A thesis-break variable is persistent failure to turn the expanded capital base into collected sales. A repeat year of negative underlying operating cash after adjusting only demonstrable classification movements, together with further property advances or increasing bank dependence, would weaken both CAP and CASH. Verified overdue statutory dues, covenant breaches, material auditor qualifications or unexplained customer balances could move gates from Conditional/Hold to Fail. Conversely, a quoted price fall alone does not prove impairment if funded, profitable operations continue. Separating market volatility from actual funding and earnings deterioration is essential in this thinly traded security. The adverse case is credible enough to justify D 3 even though reported interest coverage and net-debt/EBITDA appear comfortable.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold share-price outcome in five years requires approximately 37.97% annualized appreciation; tenfold requires 58.49%. Neither follows from a 20% recent revenue-growth rate or a nominally low P/E. At the entry quote, the corresponding terminal prices are ₹279.25 and ₹558.50. With the assumed full option pool, common-equity values would need to exceed roughly ₹551 crore and ₹1,102 crore, respectively, before adding any senior claims. This is a scale claim about future economic value, not merely a statement that the current market capitalization is small.

As a deliberately simplified benchmark, holding EBITDA margin at 29%, terminal EV/EBITDA at six times and allowing no surplus terminal cash requires revenue of roughly ₹325 crore for 5× and ₹642 crore for 10× after the modeled remaining debt and other claims, net of option exercise cash. That benchmark omits the extra funding and dilution that rapid expansion would likely require, so it is not a completed bull forecast. It is already above management's earlier ₹200–250 crore potential full-operation revenue discussion for the expanded setup. A route beyond that scale would require another capacity, customer and capital cycle that has not been evidenced. [S7 pp4–5; model inputs.]

The explicit bull model reaches ₹152.89 crore sales and a conditional ₹209.26 share value, below 5× despite a higher eight-times terminal multiple and better collections. It is useful precisely because it does not call every promising small-cap a multibagger. A 5× outcome would need stronger sustained execution, much better capital turnover, additional funded capacity or a richer exit valuation than the base assumptions. A 10× thesis would compound those demands. Neither is the central evidence-backed investment case at this cutoff.

There is also a path-dependence issue: growth financed at unfavorable prices can raise enterprise value without producing proportionate per-share returns. Employee options and possible rescue equity already demonstrate that effect in smaller examples. No probability is assigned to 5× or 10× because the necessary customer economics, mature unit capacity and financing terms are absent. The correct conclusion is that such outcomes are possible in principle but not supported as a planning assumption by this research, rather than either promising them or declaring them mathematically impossible.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
The first priority is current liquidity. Obtain the latest bank balances, fixed-deposit restrictions, sanctioned limits, actual drawings, eligible drawing power, renewal conditions and remaining committed capex. Baselines are March cash ₹0.0847 crore, deposits ₹2.4229 crore and gross debt ₹13.9356 crore, not an October cash estimate. A verified funding bridge covering the next twelve months is the milestone for reconsidering G3 Hold. A bank recall, overdue statutory amount or material unfinanced commitment is an immediate warning, not something to wait for the next annual report to assess.

Second, track collection quality using average receivable days, actual subsequent receipts and customer aging. Baselines are 187.7 average days and ₹31.71 crore closing receivables, with roughly ₹11.93 crore older than six months in the total row. Two comparable periods of improvement toward below 150 days would be constructive; further deterioration above 200 average days or rising doubtful balances without clear provisioning would be adverse. These thresholds are research triggers, not contractual covenants. Ask for a corrected age schedule rather than assuming missing digits explain every discrepancy.

Third, monitor inventory and production conversion. FY26 inventory is ₹9.67 crore, including substantial WIP and finished goods. Growth in inventory faster than accepted revenue requires order-level explanation and evidence that customers will accept the output. Fourth, verify commissioning and statutory operating permissions for D-3 and any new fire-door line, with dates and remaining spending. The May 2026 partial-commissioning statement is the baseline; an announcement of capacity alone is not equivalent to commercial production at economic utilization. Fifth, reconcile order execution: Gainwell's ₹2.925 crore ex-tax order and Utkal's ₹2.2672 crore tax-inclusive order should be tracked separately through dispatch, acceptance, invoicing and collection. Utkal's disclosed shipment and installation dates provide concrete milestones. [S8; S10–S11.]

Sixth, measure underlying cash conversion. FY26 CFO of ₹0.5040 crore and the weak three-year conversion range are baselines. Seek positive cash after all ordinary operating needs, not improvement created by reclassification or a nonrecurring asset sale. Seventh, monitor incremental capital productivity: operating capital is about ₹87.80 crore, and the latest-year normalized incremental-return proxy is 9.22%. Improvement should arise from actual operating profit and reduced working-capital intensity, not from deleting inconvenient capital from the denominator. Eighth, reconcile option grants, vesting, exercise prices and expense recognition against the authorized 939,500-share pool; no-grant and full-pool cases have materially different returns.

Ninth, track reporting discipline and capital allocation: explanations for penal charges, clean cash-flow comparatives, related-party movements, management remuneration and new property advances. The research would improve more from one complete cash and capex reconciliation than from another broad growth presentation. These are proposed checkpoints for future authorized updates, not a claim that automated monitoring, company outreach or a trade has been set up. No contact with management or external communication was undertaken for this dossier.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
The classification is “Capacity-ramp/value candidate; research hold pending funding evidence.” It is not a demonstrated compounder, income investment or supported high-return opportunity. Final BQS 4.78 and capped GQS 5.00 indicate mixed business quality and impaired growth-to-cash realization despite good historical revenue growth. IAS is NS because R cannot be supported with the current funding information. The completed-score matrix is therefore not applied as if a missing return score were zero, average or the conditional model's 14.11%. [Score audit and gate register.]

For a prospective investor, the next action is to resolve bank headroom, deposit access, remaining capex and collection timing before treating any entry price as actionable. The model's ₹53.72 base entry price at a 15% hurdle is a conditional calculation only. Even at ₹47.23, corresponding to an 18% hurdle under the same base terminal value, missing funding evidence remains missing. Conversely, a higher quote would not lower historical BQS or GQS; it would affect valuation and the eventual IAS. The three questions of business quality, growth quality and investment attractiveness remain separate.

For an existing holder, a thin quote and high lot size mean that exit feasibility should be evaluated before placing any order. ₹500,000 corresponds to 8.95 lots, which is not an executable quantity: eight lots cost ₹446,800 and nine cost ₹502,650 at the reference close. The canonical 5% continuous-turnover exit estimate is about 7.97 sessions, but the median 60-session volume allows zero whole lots at a strict 5% participation rate. Actual historical nine-lot windows took a median ten sessions among completed windows, with a seventeen-session worst completed window and one right-censored late start. No recommendation assumes the current best bid can absorb the position. [S3–S5; liquidity files.]

The company can earn a better classification if the expanded plant generates accepted, paid sales without another adverse financing cycle. Evidence would need to show functioning permissions, reliable capacity economics, two-period collection improvement and a complete capital-and-liability bridge. A worsening combination of uncollected revenue, additional property spending and bank dependence would move the assessment in the opposite direction. This action category is conditional research guidance, not a trade instruction or individualized allocation. Holdings, risk budget and tax context were not supplied. It is also one company in a larger universe, so no claim about the best SME or an overall portfolio winner is justified.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The principal evidence is the FY26 annual report, the September 2024 NSE-hosted red-herring prospectus, the FY25 annual report, the May 2026 exchange results, company earnings-call transcripts and dated NSE corporate disclosures. Official exchange bhavcopies, the security master and the surveillance register establish the quote, share identity, lot and observed trading. The source ledger supplies direct URLs, document dates, page locators, local retained files and SHA-256 hashes. Evidence types distinguish verified disclosure, reproducible calculation, management statement and analyst assumption. A disclosed statement is not automatically an independently verified outcome. The financial statements were read with their notes; the FY25 scanned report and material older pages were OCR-extracted, and critical FY26 fixed-asset and receivable schedules were visually checked.

The 60-session liquidity reconstruction independently extracts ENVIRO by exact ISIN from raw NSE archives covering 24 July–19 October 2026. Holidays are excluded by actual exchange files, not filled with invented zero-volume days. All 60 observed sessions have prints. Mean/median turnover is ₹21.2805/₹12.5540 lakh for 60 sessions and ₹27.7273/₹16.1435 lakh for 20. At 2%, 5% and 10% participation, canonical 60-session continuous exits are 19.91, 7.97 and 3.98 sessions. Whole-lot capacity is respectively 16, 64 and 157 lots across the sample, with eligible sessions only 10, 27 and 44. The 5% median-session capacity is zero; order-book spreads and executable bid depth are not disclosed by end-of-day archives. No-trade frequency is zero here, but that does not prove continuous liquidity. [S3–S5.]

The official surveillance row is active SM and does not mark ASM, GSM or ESM applicability in the parsed fields. It does flag fewer than 100 average daily unique PANs, irregular SME trading, and large historical high-low variation criteria (over 100% in six months and the specified 200%/150% annual criteria). Those official warnings coexist with prints in all 60 reconstructed sessions: regular daily prints are not the same as a broad or orderly market. The applicable-field convention is 0, while 100 means not applicable. These are warning criteria, not invented circuit limits or proof of suspension. The master price-band fields are retained as dated master data rather than interpreted as a guaranteed live execution range. A market-making framework does not promise an exit in the required size or at the last close. Raw archive hashes, extraction scripts, exact rows and rolling lot-window calculations are retained so another reviewer can reproduce these conclusions without using a market-data aggregator. L 4 starts from the lower continuous-exit band score of 5 and deducts one point jointly for lot discontinuity, official trading/volatility warnings and unverified execution conditions, not for an invented spread estimate.

The major unresolved items are current bank headroom and deposit release; permission and capex completion status; order-level margin and collection evidence; corrected receivable and cash-flow schedules; the detailed rationale for finance-cost penalties; current customer concentration; updated complete ownership and option-grant ledgers; and independent asset realizability. No current funding certificate, customer confirmation or private bank statement was available. A full facility approval cannot be inferred from March borrowing balances. Unrecorded contingencies, guarantees or lease obligations are not assumed zero merely because the retained statements do not quantify an additional claim.

Model assumptions matter most in collections, completion spending, ongoing bank rollover, operating margin, dilution and the terminal multiple. All five annual rows are saved, including cash before any rescue, opening liabilities paid once, debt movements, capex, working capital and terminal claims. The hypothetical rescue is stored separately from ordinary scenarios. Exact Decimal arithmetic governs all score contributions, missing-data bounds and half-up display rounding. Floating-point scenario arithmetic is checked within explicit tolerances and is not used to round the scorecard. The current source-free archives retain the dossier, scripts, model outputs, selected safe evidence and provenance, but exclude original issuer documents. They reproduce calculations, not a fresh audit of omitted primary sources; source re-verification requires retrieving originals from the retained URLs and checking their hashes. No brokerage action or external solicitation is included.

model_limitations: Illustrative anniversary periods use the March 2026 audited anchor, not an invented October balance sheet.
No verified current bank headroom, rollover commitment, deposit release or remaining capex certificate is available.
All supported investable returns remain null even for internally cash-positive illustrative cases.
Ordinary scenarios with a cash-floor breach have null return. Equity rescue is a separate hypothetical financing path.
Opening income-tax, current gratuity and card balances are paid once; security deposit, long gratuity and deferred-tax reserve are deducted once at terminal value.
Trade creditors, customer advances and ordinary payroll/statutory liabilities remain in operating working capital; ordinary turnover is assumed, not permanent nonpayment.
All option-pool exercise at the minimum price is a scenario, not a verified outstanding-grant count; proceeds arrive only at the endpoint.
Unrestricted status of fixed deposits is not established; ordinary cases exclude them from cash and terminal surplus, with a separate full-release sensitivity.
The tax-credit offset and vehicle-principal schedule are assumptions; liabilities and tax reserves are not a liquidation waterfall.
The model retains cash at terminal value and pays no dividends, avoiding duplicate distribution value.
Terminal multiples, margins, growth, working-capital ratios and completion capex are analyst assumptions. No unknown facility is treated as committed financing.
Full scenario and sensitivity outputs are embedded here, independently of the optional downloadable model files.
